title: SSE format negotiation, structured-surrogate handoff, and reconnect recovery strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a robust, backwards-compatible approach for shipping structured outputs (including function/tool call frames) over multiple client generations using the SSE endpoint. Current clients expect simple JSONL SSE events; newer product features require richer envelopes (chunk IDs, fragment lineage, toolcall atomic markers) and safe reconnect/reassembly semantics.

Goal: Implement server- and client-facing negotiation for SSE wire format versions, a compact 'structured-surrogate' envelope for compatibility with legacy JSONL consumers, and a deterministic reconnect/checkpoint protocol that preserves function-call atomicity and structured output reassembly without doubling latency for steady-state streaming.
requirements: Wire-version negotiation via Accept-SSE-Version request header and X-SSE-Version response header
Three supported server wire formats: v1 (simple jsonl), v2 (envelope with chunk_id/seq/partial flags), v3 (transactional fragments with function-call markers)
Structured-surrogate encoding: encode structured objects into minimal JSONL-compatible surrogates for v1 clients, with rehydration metadata embedded into a server-side checkpoint log
Reconnects must support: resume token (opaque), missing fragment fetch by sequence range, and idempotent toolcall replay using toolcall_id
No breaking changes to existing SDK surface; SDKs should auto-upgrade when Accept-SSE-Version provided
Preserve low steady-state latency for v1/v2 flows (avoid additional round trips or heavy signing)
Provide observability: per-stream metrics for version negotiated, surrogate conversions, fragment repair rate
design_decisions: Use Accept-SSE-Version header (comma-separated preferred versions) rather than new query params to simplify CDN caches
Server sets X-SSE-Version in first response event to confirm negotiated version
For v1 clients: emit structured-surrogate events with event: "surrogate" type that contain a minimal placeholder and a checkpoint token referencing a server-side blob for rehydration
For v2: include chunk_id, seq, is_partial flags in the SSE data envelope (JSON), enabling clients to stitch without server-side rehydration in many cases

For v3: support transactional fragments with explicit toolcall_start/toolcall_end events and an atomic toolcall_id; reconnect will request any missing seq ranges and the server will replay fragments deterministically
Avoid client-required crypto: checkpoints are opaque stable tokens (monotonic sequence + server shard id). Optional HMAC is planned for high-security deployments but is not required in runtime-1.22
Use base64 payloads for non-utf8 or binary structured attachments to remain JSON-safe across older clients
implementation_notes: Server-side: add VersionNegotiator component in stream gateway to inspect Accept-SSE-Version and pick best supported version for session

Gateway preserves fragment lineage metadata in an append-only checkpoint store (s3-backed) for 48h by default; the token returned to clients is small (12-16 bytes base62) referencing checkpoint entries
When emitting surrogate events: data payload contains {surrogate_type, token, preview}, where preview is a small human-readable snippet for v1 clients; full structured payload is in checkpoint store
Reconnect flow: client includes last_seq_seen and checkpoint_token on re-open; gateway validates and returns missing seq ranges as deltas (v2/v3) or surrogate replays (v1)

Toolcall atomicity: every tool invocation started on stream emits toolcall_start with toolcall_id, partial fragments reference toolcall_id, and toolcall_end marks commit. If reconnect reveals missing fragments inside a toolcall, server will resend full toolcall fragment set to ensure deterministic tool invocation replay

SDK changes (minor): expose Client.sseVersion option and transparently include Accept-SSE-Version; provide helper to rehydrate surrogate by fetching checkpoint blob when current environment supports structured outputs
Fall-back to chunked transfer (HTTP/1.1) for clients that can't use SSE, preserving same envelopes encoded as length-prefixed JSON lines
tradeoffs: Pros: surrogate approach preserves compatibility and keeps payloads small for legacy clients; v2/v3 provide richer guarantees for modern clients
Cons: checkpoint store increases storage and operational cost; surrogate rehydration requires an extra fetch for clients that opt to rehydrate, adding complexity to client libraries
We chose opaque tokens instead of public sequence signing to reduce header changes and keep performance predictable under CDN/proxy caches
test_plan: Unit tests for VersionNegotiator covering header negotiation permutations
Integration tests that simulate reconnection with gaps: 1) single missing chunk, 2) mid-toolcall missing fragments, 3) large gap spanning >1k fragments
Compatibility tests: v1 client consumes surrogate preview only; v1 client rehydrates via checkpoint fetch; v2 client stitches fragments locally; v3 client verifies toolcall atomicity
Chaos test: simulate gateway restart and checkpoint store eventual consistency delays; validate that reconnect tokens gracefully degrade to full replay fallback
Load test: measure 99p latency impact when surrogate mode enabled vs pure v2 streaming at 1000 concurrent streams
acceptance_criteria: Gateway returns X-SSE-Version and client SDK honors negotiated version in 100% of tested permutations
Reconnect successfully replays missing seq ranges for >95% of simulated gap cases without manual intervention
Toolcall atomicity preserved across reconnects: at most one successful external tool invocation per toolcall_id irrespective of reconnects
Compatibility: legacy v1 clients receive valid JSONL stream with surrogate events and do not error; rehydration path available and exercised in integration tests
Metrics emitted: stream.version, surrogate.rate, reconnect.repair_count; dashboards added to console project runtime-1.22
dependencies: SEC-1201 (optional hmac design for high-security deployments)
notes: Implementation will start behind a feature flag 'sse_wire_v3' to allow gradual rollout to dedicated clusters
Checkpoint TTL set to 48h for now; ops should evaluate cost after initial rollout and consider tiering by customer plan
We should coordinate with customer success before enabling surrogate rehydration globally since some enterprise clients may rely on exact JSONL semantics
comments: 2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial spec attached in Drive. Decided to prefer header-based negotiation to avoid query param churn.
2026-03-10 Marcus Liu: Spike complete — gateway prototype negotiates v1/v2/v3 and emits X-SSE-Version. Observed median extra CPU < 2% for v3 envelopes under 500 streams.

2026-03-11 Sophie Martin (reviewer): Reviewed design; requested clearer guarantees for toolcall-once semantics under partial replay. Suggested we implement server-side dedupe using toolcall_id and idempotency keys when invoking external tools.

2026-03-12 Marcus Liu: Added toolcall_id dedupe in implementation_notes; PR #482 includes unit tests for dedupe logic. Open question: how to surface failures when dedupe suppresses replay but upstream tool hasn't recorded call? Tracking as follow-up.

2026-03-13 Ops (Ben Rodriguez): Checkpoint store provisioning done in staging. Need to confirm lifecycle policy with cost dashboard before production rollout. Also requested a small migration runbook for cluster updates behind feature flag.
